Methylprednisolone binds to Nr3c1, a nuclear receptor involved in cortisol signaling, thereby modulating the effects of cortisol in the body. This pathway implies that Mifepristone may influence the expression or activity of Nr3c1 through its role in regulating hormone therapy agents. The lowest common ancestor of Mifepristone and Methylprednisolone is 3-Oxo-Delta(4) Steroid, indicating a shared metabolic or hormonal pathway. The evidence suggests that Mifepristone may indirectly affect Nr3c1 by influencing the hormonal environment in which it operates, though the exact mechanism remains to be fully elucidated.
